title: Away in a Manger

text.name: Anonymous
text.role: Verses 1 and 2, first printed in Philadelphia (1885)

description: Away in a Manger in Tonic Solfa to MUELLER, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, all three verses and a piano.
about: The first two verses of this children's carol were printed anonymously in Philadelphia in 1885; the third is usually credited to John Thomas McFarland. The tune MUELLER, by James Ramsey Murray, was published in 1887.
In Britain, and in many Nigerian churches, the same words are also sung to William J. Kirkpatrick's CRADLE SONG, with 'the stars in the bright sky' in the third line.
underlay: A-way in a man-ger, no crib for a bed, The lit-tle Lord Je-sus laid down His sweet head; The stars in the sky_ looked down where He lay, The lit-tle Lord Je-sus, a-sleep on the hay.

lines: Away in a manger, no crib for a bed,
The little Lord Jesus laid down His sweet head;
The stars in the sky looked down where He lay,
The little Lord Jesus, asleep on the hay.
The cattle are lowing, the Baby awakes,
But little Lord Jesus, no crying He makes;
I love Thee, Lord Jesus, look down from the sky
And stay by my cradle till morning is nigh.
Be near me, Lord Jesus, I ask Thee to stay
Close by me for ever, and love me, I pray;
Bless all the dear children in Thy tender care,
And fit us for heaven, to live with Thee there.
